_about: Appendix H: the signal-to-condition association table, referenced by FR-AI-007.
This table is the ONLY source of condition names anywhere in the system. Names are
never generated by the analysis provider and never derived from a ClinicalSignal
identifier, which describes an appearance rather than a condition.
EVERY ROW SHIPS WITH enabled: false, AND THAT IS THE INTENDED RELEASE 1.0 STATE.
FR-AI-007 permits an association list only where the row is enabled, which under
DR-009 requires a recorded precision measurement meeting the NFR-SAFE-006 bar. No
such measurement exists (OI-012), no clinical reviewer has been engaged (OI-001,
DEP-003), and OI-011 records that condition naming materially changes the product's
regulatory posture with the store health-policy review not yet performed. Enabling a
row before those are resolved would be the single most consequential unreviewed
With every row disabled the app behaves as specified in SRS v1.1: a referral shows
the observation and no condition name. The limitations statement stays accurate
because FR-ONB-007 says the app 'may list conditions that sometimes look similar',
Enabling one row later is a change to this file plus a measurement. It is not a
change to any code: the suppression logic, the fixed framing text, the equal-
prominence rendering and the audit trail are all built and all tested.
_omissions: Two ClinicalSignal identifiers have no row here, deliberately rather than pending.
IRREGULAR_LESION. A mark with an uneven edge or more than one colour is the
appearance that matters most and the one this system is least equipped to speak
about. Naming anything from a compressed phone photograph in that category risks
two opposite harms: a name that frightens someone into a needless biopsy, and a
name reassuring enough that they do not go. Neither is acceptable and there is no
wording that avoids both. The observation plus a referral is the whole of what this
system should say, so there is nothing here for FR-AI-008 to suppress.
OPEN_WOUND. Broken skin needs attention regardless of what caused it, and a
differential would not change the advice by a word. A name here would be decoration
on a referral that is already unambiguous.
A missing row resolves to SuppressionReason.NO_TABLE_ENTRY under FR-AI-008, which
displays the observation alone. The suppression is recorded on the scan log, so
these omissions are visible in the data rather than only in this comment.

_note: OI-013 is specifically about this row. Pigmentary findings are difficult to
distinguish on darker skin tones, and whether these names can reach the 80%
precision bar in NFR-SAFE-006 is unknown. This is the row most likely to stay
disabled permanently, and the last that should be enabled.
